blogs.title: Beyond Euclidean Distance: Why Angles Matter More Than Magnitude in AI Image Generation
blogs.description: This post demystifies the core theoretical insight of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT). It explains why traditional finetuning methods focus on keeping weight changes small (Euclidean distance) and why that approach often fails to preserve an AI model's original creativity. Using the analogy of image phase vs. magnitude spectra, we'll explore how OFT focuses on preserving the 'angles' between neurons to maintain semantic meaning while allowing the model to learn new styles or subjects.

blogs.title: DreamBooth vs. OFT: How to Teach AI New Subjects Without Forgetting Everything Else
blogs.description: Focusing on the 'subject-driven generation' application, this article compares the new OFT method against popular existing techniques like DreamBooth and LoRA. We will break down real-world examples where older methods cause 'model collapse' (forgetting how to generate other objects) or fail to capture specific details. The post highlights how OFT achieves faster convergence and higher stability, allowing users to train custom models with fewer images and less trial-and-error.

blogs.title: Total Control Without the Bloat: Introducing Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT)
blogs.description: This post tackles the 'controllable generation' challenge, such as turning sketches into photos or enforcing specific poses. It introduces Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT), a variation of OFT that adds strict boundaries to prevent the model from drifting too far from its original knowledge. Readers will learn how COFT outperforms heavy architectures like ControlNet by offering superior precision and image fidelity without adding any extra computational cost during image generation.

blogs.title: The Efficiency Paradox: Getting Better AI Results with Fewer Parameters
blogs.description: A deep dive into the technical architecture of OFT, simplified for developers and tech enthusiasts. This article explains how OFT uses 'block-diagonal orthogonal matrices' to drastically reduce the number of trainable parameters compared to Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). We will discuss how this mathematical trick creates a smoother optimization landscape, leading to quicker training times and a final model that runs just as fast as the original pretrained version.
